Supplemental peer evidence for PR #280 at c8d2eab2fc9e073d8c8b8de27dbb53e8141ec315.

The one-shot F232 binder receipt arrived after security verdict 8d26e766696584d1536d566177153abd28478ae5. This note supplies the requested late evidence; it does not change that final-round PASS WITH NOTES or reopen F232 as a block.

Correctness reviewer reported an isolated diagnostic against this head, run through shared-build for -p pij-daemon --lib with selector:
codex_bind::tests::reviewer_one_busy_probe_is_not_retried_after_release -- --exact --nocapture

The supplied log was inspected. It records four cargo jobs/four test threads and one passing test, zero failures, in 0.04 s. The binder logged a transient pane-query error saying another process was attaching and nothing was launched. The diagnostic then reported 30 unchanged ticks without retry; an unrelated new thread triggered successful binding.

Peer-reported counter detail: the first pane_pid Err caused zero bind_once calls, the seat remained unbound through 30 quiet ticks, and an unrelated thread/lock-set change caused one bind_once call. This corroborates the source trace: saving Seen before a failed probe consumes the retry trigger. It does not show a false absence, unauthorized binding, or tombstone.

The reviewer also reported the exact-head new contention regression passing 20/20. That separate repeat count is attributed to the reviewer and is not claimed as security execution or as a count from the one-test binder log.

F232 remains the named non-blocking C34 follow-up under pm-001's ruling: avoid marking a row/lock set seen when its pane probe errs. S280-001 remains the separate carried permission follow-up. Security performed no fresh code review, test execution, mutation, deployment or live-fleet contention for this supplement.
